title: Ilocos Gold Melon (Ilocos Gold F1): Characteristics
metaDescription: Ilocos Gold melon is an F1 hybrid (honeydew) melon variety. See its days to harvest, yield, pest ratings, traits and where it grows best.
excerpt: Ilocos Gold melon is an F1 hybrid (honeydew) melon variety, also sold or known as Ilocos Gold F1 or Ilocos Gold honeydew. It is not a registered variety, so the facts here come from its seller and farm sources. It comes from Known You Seed (sold in the Philippines through Harbest Agribusiness).

heroImage.alt: Ampalaya seedlings planted through plastic mulch on raised beds, the kind of farm where Ilocos Gold melon is grown

blocks.text: If you came here looking for Ilocos Gold F1 or Ilocos Gold honeydew, this is the same melon. The facts below come from its seller and from farm sources, each one listed at the end. Compare it with the others in our [melon variety finder](/crop-varieties/melon), or see [every crop variety](/crop-varieties) we list. For the crop itself, read our guide: [Land preparation for gourds and melons](/land-preparation/cucurbit-land-preparation).

Days to harvest, per the seller

blocks.text: How long does it take, and how much does it yield?

Days to harvest, by the seller's count: 60 to 65 days after sowing. No trial on record checks this figure yet, so treat it as the seller's own and compare with farms near you before you plan a season around it.

Once you know the day count, anee.io dates every task from each lot's own planting day, with [the growth stages and weather](/features/growth-stages-and-weather) beside it.
Is it resistant to pests and diseases?
No pest or disease ratings are published for this variety. So treat it as untested, and scout every week.

The pests and diseases that hit melon fields most often: [anthracnose](/diseases/anthracnose), [cutworm](/pests/cutworm), [damping off](/diseases/damping-off), [downy mildew of cucurbits](/diseases/downy-mildew), [Fusarium wilt](/diseases/fusarium-wilt). Our [pest finder](/pests) and [disease finder](/diseases) help you name what you see.
What its seller and farm sources say

items: **Days to harvest:** 60 to 65 days after sowing.
**Fruit:** Small oval fruit with white flesh, 600 g to 1 kg, brix 12 to 15.

blocks.text: Why farmers know it: named among the honeydews most commonly planted in the Philippines, in Harbest's current catalogue. These are the seller's own figures, from its own trials. So plant a small area first, and compare it with your usual melon on the same ground.
Where and when to plant Ilocos Gold melon

Muskmelon and honeydew need dry weather near harvest, or the fruit cracks and loses its sweetness. Plant so that the fruit ripens before the rains. Before planting, get the field ready with our guide: [Pagtatanim ng gulay](/crops/pagtatanim-ng-gulay).

items.q: Is Ilocos Gold F1 the same as Ilocos Gold?
items.a: Yes. Ilocos Gold F1 is another name for Ilocos Gold. Seed sellers use both, so ask for either one.
No. It is a hybrid, so seed saved from it does not grow true and yields less. Buy new seed each season.

items.q: Where can I buy seed of Ilocos Gold?
items.a: Ask an accredited seed dealer in your province, the seller named on this page or your municipal agriculturist. Look for the certified seed tag or a sealed pack before you pay.
